column2: Two glucoses joined in an unusual way, named after koji, the mould used to make sake, soy sauce and miso. It turns up in small amounts in honey and sake.
Also called D-psicose, and marketed as a "rare sugar" because it occurs naturally only in tiny amounts, in figs and raisins. It's on so many low-sugar labels now that it's hardly rare as an answer.
